draft.title: Causes of river decline in the Murray-Darling Basin
card: The Murray-Darling Basin is a huge river system in south-eastern Australia. Its rivers are in poor health because of several pressures that often act together.
Water extraction
Taking water for irrigation and towns leaves less in the rivers. Less water flows along the river and into wetlands.
Dams and weirs
These hold water back and release it when people need it. This changes the natural pattern of flows, so the floods and low flows that native species rely on happen at the wrong times or not at all.
Land clearing

Removing native vegetation from the land beside rivers can let more soil and salt wash into them. Drought, a long period of low rainfall, cuts the water entering the rivers and adds to the other pressures.
draft.remember: Less water taken, changed flows, cleared land and drought all harm the Basin's rivers.

a.q: Which of these is a human action that has reduced the health of the Basin's rivers?
opts: Taking water out of rivers for irrigation
A long period of low rainfall across the Basin
Natural floods spreading over a wetland
Native trees growing beside a river bank
a.why: Taking water for irrigation leaves less in the rivers, which harms their health. Drought also reduces river health, but it is a natural period of low rainfall, not an action people take.
a.clue: Look for something people do, not something the weather does.

b.q: A dam on a Basin river holds back water in spring and releases it in summer for farms downstream. Why might this harm native fish?
opts: It changes the natural timing of flows they rely on
It adds more water than the river has ever held
It stops farmers from taking any water from the river
It clears the native plants from the river bank
b.why: Dams and weirs change the natural pattern of flows. Native species rely on floods at certain times, so holding water back in spring can disrupt breeding. The dam does not clear land, and it supplies water to farms rather than stopping them from taking it.
b.clue: Think about when the river would naturally flood.

a.best: Taking water out of rivers for irrigation

b.best: It changes the natural timing of flows they rely on

problems.detail: 'Less water taken' says the opposite of the card. Taking too much water harms the rivers, not taking less. It should read something like 'Too much water taken' or 'Water extraction'.
Drought is placed inside the 'Land clearing' bullet, so it could read as part of land clearing. It would be clearer as its own pressure.
